newsitem.title: CHINA: China B shares up on new issue, selective buying.
newsitem.headline: China B shares up on new issue, selective buying.

text.p: Hard currency B shares on the Shanghai stock exchange closed up on Friday on healthy trading volume, buoyed by buying of newcomer Inner Mongolia Yitai Coal Co Ltd, brokers said.
The Shanghai B index share rose 0.741 points or 1.00 percent to 74.923 points with turnover of $25.726 million compared with $7.132 million on Thursday.

In Shenzhen, the B share market ended up due to sporadic selective buying by institutions with the B index gaining 1.49 points or 1.15 percent to 131.48 points on turnover of HK$44 million against HK$45 million, brokers said.

Brokers said the rise in Shanghai's B share trading volume could be a sign the B share market was starting a new upward trend, due to improved sentiment on talk of new government moves to reform state firms, which could boost some listed companies.
The recent strength of H shares -- shares of Chinese companies listed in Hong Kong -- could also carry over into the Shanghai B share market, they said.
"The H share market should have a rest after sharp rises over the past few weeks, so the B shares will rise on fresh inflow of capital," one local broker said.
Yitai Coal closed at $0.470, up $0.063 or 15.48 percent compared with an offer price of $0.407.
Foreign capital was seen entering the market, chasing after the share issue, brokers said.
Shanghai Diesel Engine Co was the biggest gainer among old shares, surging $0.024 or 9.68 percent to $0.272 on a technical rebound, traders said.
Analysts said market sentiment was weak in Shenzhen.
"Buying interest remained weak," an analyst at J&A Securities (HK) said.

But the analyst said that recently listed B shares, such as Beijing Orient, were likely to outperform the market on investor expectations that they would post robust results in the 1997 interim corporate reporting season ending August 30.
Beijing Orient added HK$0.05 to HK$4.00 after 1.88 million shares were traded. It was the day's second most actively traded B share issue.

The firm, a maker of lamps and colour television components, earlier this week posted net profits of 68.72 million yuan for January-June 1997 under international accounting standards, up 29 percent from the year-earlier period.
"The stock may become the market's star later this year, backed by its solid earnings," the J&A analyst said.
Investors may continue to hold back from large-scale trading this month, waiting for all B share companies to release their interim results, an analyst at Everbright Securities said.
Shenzhen Special Economic Zone Real Estate & Properties was the best performer on Friday, surging HK$0.17 or 7.02 percent to HK$2.59 on volume of 42,000 shares.
Brokers said institutions had been supporting Bengang, which was still traded below its offer price of HK$2.38 per share.
On the domestic stock markets, Shanghai's A share index ended up 6.988 points or 0.56 percent to 1,262.179 points on turnover of 5.728 billion yuan against 3.074 billion yuan.
Shenzhen's A index lost 3.56 points or 0.87 percent to 403.83, with turnover expanding to 6.2 billion yuan from Thursday's 4.4 billion.
